about: #27's budgets (AC3), with the numbers the owner approved on 2026-10-31 from docs/performance/baseline-1.4.0.md. No script writes this file: it changes only by review, and a number over a row goes back to the owner through the lead, never raised by the lane. docs/performance/budgets.md says how each gate runs and what fails it.

reference.about: The frozen package the timing and heap runs measure against, twice a round: v1.4.0 built with its own lockfile and build (npm run perf:reference). The digest is a SHA-256 over its files sorted by path (scripts/perf-probe.js packageDigest), and npm run perf:probe --baseline refuses a run whose first or second package isn't it.

timing.rule: Paired and interleaved: each run times the frozen 1.4.0 package twice and the candidate once a round, rotated, at least 12 rounds per profile and a multiple of the package count. It fails when the candidate's median ratio to the mean of the two 1.4.0 runs is over 1 + tolerancePct / 100, and it's invalid when 1.4.0 against itself is more than tolerancePct off. Absolute ms are recorded beside it, not gated.
timing.modeAbout: gate since 2026-10-31, under the rule it reported by until then: gate after 10 CI runs if 1.4.0 against itself stayed within 7% on at least 9 and the invalid-run check would have passed. The perf workflow ran on 14 pushes to next, f7a17e5e to 7489d7b3, and all 14 were valid: the worst 1.4.0-against-itself median was +2.6% on typical and -2.2% on maximal. A timing fail, or an invalid run, now fails CI's perf job. The perf job isn't in pr-gate's needs or any ruleset, so it blocks no merge; making it block one is the owner's call (docs/performance/budgets.md).

heap.modeAbout: gate since 2026-11-01, at today's heap plus about 5%, the rule the owner approved for the byte rows; the coordinator decided it for the owner, who can reverse it. CI's 1.4.0 heap (3.94 to 3.98 MiB over 14 runs on next) matches the Mac's (3.94 to 4.01) within about 1%, so a MiB number means the same on both. Set again on 2026-11-01, when the probe began reading the heap once the writes its own key sets off have committed (#152): the 2.81 it replaces was CI's 2.68 MiB on 7489d7b3, read at the echo, while the key's save was still in flight. On the same tree, next at 2ae3f528, CI's old probe read 2.685 MiB on typical (perf run 41354479082) and the fixed one 2.96 and 2.95, so the row moved for the probe, not for code. With the fixed probe, CI read next three times on typical, 2.96 and 2.95 MiB at 2ae3f528 and 2.94 at ecc401a7 (perf runs 41355105542, 41357548903 and 41359820583), and 2.68, 2.68 and 2.66 on maximal: their median, 2.95, x 1.05 is 3.0975, so 3.10, failing above 3.19 with the 3%. Set again on 2026-11-02, on the NTN-17 stack's top, once the probe typed its key again only on the page's own word (#157): before, it typed it again when no echo reached it within 50 ms, so a page busy starting got a second key, and its second save read about 0.05 MiB high. With one key a round, CI read next's code at 0caa9c3e three times on typical, 3.12, 3.12 and 3.12 MiB (perf runs 41397951120, 41398738770 and 41416198332), and 2.86, 2.86 and 2.86 on maximal: their median, 3.12, x 1.05 is 3.276, so 3.28, failing above 3.378 with the 3%. The 3.10 it replaces was next's 2.95 before #121, #131, #134 and #147, whose own growth the fixed probe read locally as +0.056, +0.036, +0.049 and +0.023 MiB on typical. One number gates both profiles, so maximal has more room. A heap fail, or an invalid run, fails CI's perf job, which isn't in pr-gate's needs or any ruleset, so it blocks no merge.
